input.question: Why doesn't Disney just buy back the rights?
input.ground_truth: Contracts. 20th Century Fox currently has distribution deal for Fantastic Four films, so trying to break that deal might have some negative consequences that Disney might not want to bother with. Also, it's worth pointing out that as far as Marvel's roster of superheroes go, the Fantastic Four are pretty craptastic. The money makers for Marvel have always been heroes like Spider-Man, the Hulk, Iron Man, and Captain America. This is why we're seeing Disney so focused on the Avengers and the heroes that make up the team. Not many people are clamoring to see the Fantastic Four in action (especially after those first two movies), so Disney probably doesn't care enough to make an offer to buy the rights back. Now, if we were talking about someone like Spider-Man, Disney would probably shell out the cash. I just have a hard time imagining that the Fantastic Four is high up on the company's priority list.

That sounds like a wonderful and thoughtful morning routine! Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Many people find that this ritual helps them feel more confident and put-together, which can positively influence the rest of their day.

If you enjoy the process, there’s no need to rush it. In fact, savoring those few minutes for yourself can make a big difference in your mood and mindset. Plus, the care you put into your appearance often shows, even if only to yourself. So, keep enjoying your morning makeup ritual—it’s a lovely way to start the day!

Okay! Imagine you have a really cool toy that you let your friend play with for a while. But then, your friend says, "Now I get to keep this toy forever, and you can't have it back, even if you want it." 

Disney tried to let someone else play with one of their stories (like a movie or a character) for a little while, but now that friend says, "No, I'm not giving it back, even if you ask nicely or give me money." 

So, Disney can't just buy the toy (or the story) back because the friend (the other company) isn't willing to sell it anymore. That's why Disney can't just buy the rights back.
